title: Temporal Diffraction Grating for Engineered Superconducting Qubit Dissipation
authors: Pratik J. Barge, Kater W. Murch
abstract: Parametric frequency modulation is a standard tool in superconducting circuits for activating tunable interactions and implementing quantum gates. Here, we engineer dissipation in a flux-tunable transmon qubit by using sideband modulation to bring it into resonance with a lossy resonator, opening an on-demand Purcell decay channel. We find that pulsing this channel on and off does not simply lower the time-averaged decay rate; instead, it reorganizes the dissipation spectrum into a structured interference pattern. A Chebyshev-propagator model for the repeated on/off block reproduces the measured spectra and reveals a close structural correspondence to N-slit Fraunhofer diffraction, with each on-window acting as a temporal aperture. By varying the pulse duration and duty cycle, we demonstrate control over the spacing, contrast, and envelope of the dissipation spectrum. These results establish pulsed parametric modulation as a direct method for shaping engineered dissipation in superconducting circuits and provide a new control knob for open quantum system dynamics.
summary: The paper demonstrates that by rapidly pulsing the parametric modulation coupling between a transmon qubit and a resonator, one can engineer structured interference patterns into the qubit's decay spectrum. This technique treats pulsed modulation as an effective temporal aperture, providing unprecedented control over open quantum system dynamics beyond simple average decay rates.
main_problem: The research aims to move beyond simple time-averaged descriptions of qubit decay by engineering structured dissipation spectra in superconducting qubits.
main_result: Pulsing the parametric modulation channel reorganizes the engineered dissipation spectrum into a distinct, controllable interference pattern analogous to N-slit diffraction.
method: The authors use a Chebyshev-propagator model applied to the time evolution governed by alternating 'on' and 'off' coupling periods.
model_or_system: The system is a flux-tunable transmon qubit coupled dispersively to a lossy resonator. Control is achieved via parametric frequency modulation, which is pulsed on and off.
key_observables: Excited-state probability ($P_e$) and the structured dissipation spectrum measured by sweeping the modulation detuning ($\Delta_m/2\pi$).
important_parameters: Pulse duration ($	au_{on}, 	au_{off}$), duty cycle, and the total cycle time ($t_c = 	au_{on} + 	au_{off}$).
main_assumptions: The off-segment Hamiltonian assumes negligible coupling ($g_{	ext{off}} \approx 0$) and only accounts for resonator decay ($\kappa$).
figures_summary: Figures compare continuous vs. pulsed modulation spectra, showing multiple interference dips for the latter; one figure illustrates $P_e$ evolution over time.
paper_structure: The paper develops from describing the physical setup and the limitations of simple averaging to deriving the full block propagator ($M$), calculating its N-th power using Chebyshev polynomials, and finally mapping the resulting probability structure onto a diffraction grating analogy.
why_interesting: This work provides a novel, time-domain control knob for open quantum systems dynamics in superconducting circuits, allowing precise spectral shaping of engineered dissipation channels.
